Code refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of code without changing its external behavior. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and more readable. This often involves renaming variables, breaking long functions into smaller ones, or simplifying complex logic. Refactoring does not add new features—it simply improves how existing code is written.

Over time, code can become messy and difficult to understand. This mess is called technical debt. If left unmanaged, technical debt makes it harder to fix bugs or add new features. Regular refactoring helps reduce this debt, making the code easier to maintain and less confusing for developers. A well-structured codebase saves time and effort in the long run.
